events.title: VMware 1.0 released
events.summary: VMware shipped version 1.0 on May 15, 1999 for Linux — desktop software that ran multiple x86 operating systems in virtual machines (the Windows port followed in November 1999).
events.about: VMware let developers test on Linux, Windows, and BSD simultaneously on one PC — no rebooting, no spare hardware. It pioneered x86 binary translation and later hardware-assisted virtualization. DevOps teams later built on the same hypervisor lineage for ESXi and cloud VMs; Docker containers addressed a different layer, but VMware defined how backend devs thought about isolation.

narrative.whyChosen: VMware Workstation brought practical x86 virtualization to developer desktops.
narrative.whyImportant: It made cross-platform testing and server simulation routine before cloud VMs were ubiquitous.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed to run multiple OS environments without maintaining separate physical machines.

events.title: OpenCart first released
events.summary: Christopher G. Mann published the first public OpenCart release on May 11, 1999 — a Perl-based open-source shopping cart.
events.about: OpenCart later moved to PHP and became a popular self-hosted e-commerce platform — lightweight compared to Magento, with extensions for payments and shipping. It competes with WooCommerce and PrestaShop for small-to-mid merchants who want to own their store code.

narrative.whyChosen: OpenCart is one of the longest-running open-source e-commerce projects.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave merchants a free alternative to hosted storefronts before Shopify dominated SMB retail.
narrative.problemSolved: Small retailers needed affordable cart software without enterprise licensing fees.
